stem.en: Why do animals with external fertilisation generally produce more eggs than animals with internal fertilisation?

text.en: Many of their eggs are eaten or carried off

feedback.en: Yes. A large number of eggs are lost in open water.

text.en: Their bodies are larger than those of other animals

feedback.en: Body size does not explain egg number here.

text.en: Their eggs need no sperm to develop into young

feedback.en: These eggs do need sperm. Sperm meet them in the water.

text.en: Their young stay protected in the mother's body

feedback.en: That describes internal fertilisation, where fewer eggs are produced.

explanation.en: In external fertilisation the eggs lie in open water. Many are destroyed by currents or eaten by other animals, and animals that produce many eggs still leave some young.

hints.en: Where are the eggs after they are laid?
What can happen to an egg in open water?
